title: Physics 1 formula reference
intro: Liminal's own summary of the relations used in this course, grouped by the question each one answers. Each row gives the relation, what it means in words, and the SI units involved. Relations between vectors hold component by component, so choose a positive direction before using them.

rows.meaning: Gravitational field strength (free-fall acceleration) near Earth's surface; use 10 m/s^2 only when a question says so.
Universal gravitational constant.
Air pressure at sea level.
Density of fresh water.
Converting between revolutions, radians and degrees.
Average velocity is displacement per unit time; it is the slope of a position–time graph.
Average acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time; it is the slope of a velocity–time graph.

rows.relation: Δx = area under a v–t graph
rows.meaning: Signed area between a velocity graph and the time axis gives displacement; Δv is the area under an a–t graph.
Velocity after time t when the acceleration is constant.
Position after time t when the acceleration is constant.
Links speed and displacement for constant acceleration when time is not given.

rows.relation: v_x = v cos θ, v_y = v sin θ
rows.meaning: Components of a velocity at angle θ above the +x axis; a projectile's v_x stays constant and its a_y = −g.
Relative velocity: the velocity of A relative to C is A's velocity relative to B plus B's velocity relative to C (as vectors).
The net external force on a system equals its mass times its acceleration; apply it along each axis. Zero net force means constant velocity.
Third law: the forces two objects exert on each other are equal in size and opposite in direction, and act on different objects.
Center of mass of a system; only external forces change its motion.
Gravitational attraction between two masses whose centers are r apart.
Gravitational field strength at distance r from the center of a body of mass M, and the weight of a mass m there.
Static friction adjusts up to a maximum; kinetic friction is fixed by the normal force. Both act along the surface, opposing slipping.
An ideal spring pulls or pushes back toward its natural length with a force proportional to the stretch or compression x.
Acceleration toward the center of a circle of radius r; the net inward force must equal ma_c.
Speed of uniform circular motion with period T.

groups.title: Where does the energy go? (work, energy and power)

rows.meaning: Translational kinetic energy.
Work by a constant force F over a displacement d, where θ is the angle between them; for a varying force, W is the area under the F–x graph.
Work–energy theorem: the net work on an object changes its kinetic energy.
Change in gravitational potential energy of an object–Earth system near the surface.
Gravitational potential energy of two masses r apart, taken as zero when they are very far apart.
Energy stored in an ideal spring stretched or compressed by x.
Energy accounting for a chosen system: work by outside forces changes its kinetic, potential and internal energy. Friction inside the system gives ΔE_int = f_k d.
Power is the rate of energy transfer.
Instantaneous power delivered by a force F to an object moving at velocity v.
Linear momentum, a vector in the direction of the velocity.
Impulse: a force acting over a time interval changes momentum; J is the area under an F–t graph.
A system's total momentum is constant when the net external force on it is zero (or negligible during a brief collision).
Velocity of a system's center of mass.
Kinetic energy is also conserved only in elastic collisions; objects that stick together have the largest loss of kinetic energy.
Angular velocity and angular acceleration; the constant-acceleration motion relations hold with θ, ω and α in place of x, v and a.
Speed and tangential acceleration of a point at distance r from the axis.
Torque of a force F applied at distance r from the axis at angle θ to the line from the axis; r_⊥ is the lever arm.
Rotational inertia of point masses about an axis. Common shapes about a central axis: hoop MR^2, solid disk or cylinder (1/2)MR^2, solid sphere (2/5)MR^2, rod (1/12)ML^2 (center) or (1/3)ML^2 (end).
Rotational inertia about an axis parallel to one through the center of mass, a distance d away.
Second law in rotational form. Equilibrium needs both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0 about any axis.
Rotational kinetic energy; a rolling object has both (1/2)mv^2 and (1/2)Iω^2, with v = ωR when it does not slip.
Work done by a constant torque turning through angle Δθ.
Angular momentum of a rigid object, and of a particle moving past a point at perpendicular distance r_⊥.
Angular impulse changes angular momentum; with zero net external torque, L is constant.
Period, frequency and angular frequency of a repeating motion.
Period of a mass m on an ideal spring of constant k; it does not depend on the amplitude.
Period of a simple pendulum of length L swinging through small angles.
Position in simple harmonic motion with amplitude A, starting from x = A at t = 0 (use sine when it starts at x = 0).
An oscillator's total energy; at displacement x it splits into (1/2)kx^2 and (1/2)mv^2.

groups.title: How do fluids push and flow? (fluids)

rows.meaning: Density is mass per unit volume.
Pressure is force per unit area, exerted perpendicular to a surface.
Absolute pressure at depth h below a surface at pressure P_0; ρgh alone is the gauge pressure.
Buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced; a floating object displaces its own weight.
Continuity: in steady flow of an incompressible fluid, the volume flow rate Av is the same everywhere along a pipe.
Bernoulli's equation along a streamline: where a fluid moves faster or higher, its pressure is lower. For a hole at depth h in an open tank, v = √(2gh).

rows.relation: sin θ = opp/hyp, cos θ = adj/hyp, tan θ = opp/adj
rows.meaning: Right-triangle ratios for resolving vectors into components.
Magnitude of a vector from perpendicular components.
Circumference and area of a circle.
Volume of a sphere and of a cylinder.

notes: This reference is Liminal's own arrangement and wording for learning the course. It is not a copy of College Board's equation sheet, whose selection, symbols and layout differ.
The exam supplies College Board's equation sheet; download it from the AP® Physics 1 exam page on College Board's website and practice with it before the exam.

A relation is only as good as its conditions: the constant-acceleration relations need constant a, energy conservation needs no external work and no friction losses, and momentum conservation needs no net external force.
